connections.why: Entrepreneurs spot gaps by analysing how markets behave
Understanding market structure and demand shapes marketing strategy
The legal form a business takes determines the finance it can raise
Start-up funding decisions feed into ongoing financial management
The accounts produced by the finance function are the raw material for ratio analysis
Analysing past data is the basis for forecasting future sales
Forecasts feed the decision trees and critical-path models used to choose actions
Financial analysis reveals the strengths and weaknesses a strategy must address
Strategy is the means of achieving the firm's aims and objectives
Strategic projects are tested with investment-appraisal techniques
Operational efficiency shows up in cost and profitability ratios
Managing people and culture is central to managing organisational change
Change introduces risks that must be identified and managed
Fiscal and monetary policy shift the demand and costs firms face
New technology reshapes production methods and the workforce
Legal and ethical constraints limit how products can be marketed
Global trade widens the markets and competition a firm faces
Globalisation opens strategic options like exporting and offshoring
Both are quantitative tools for choosing between competing options
Economic volatility is a key external source of business risk
